syllabus.quote: Analyse examine in detail to show meaning, identify elements and the relationship between them

one_line: Break the topic into parts. For each part, say what it leads to in the question's situation.

points.heading: Break it into points and expand them
points.text: Make a point, then expand it into what it causes or means. Some mark schemes say a proper analysis must have expansions. Two November 2022 mark schemes cap an answer with no expansion at 6 of 8. None of the 18 Analyse mark schemes from 2022 on gives a mark for a conclusion.

cites.quote: Must have expansions to be a proper analysis
Max six marks if no attempt at expansion

points.heading: Break it into points and expand them
points.text: A short description or definition at the start can earn one or two marks. After that, a description earns marks only when you use it to explain an effect or a reason.

cites.quote: Max two from: Resolution is measured/described as pixels per inch/ppi
Descriptions of vector images were not given credit unless these descriptions were used to explain why vector graphics are, or are not, used on websites.

points.heading: Break it into points and expand them
points.text: Listing features gets few marks. Expand each one.

cites.quote: The weaker answers did not go beyond listing points so could not gain many marks.

points.heading: Show the links
points.text: Show how one thing leads to another, and then to a further effect. Examiners and mark schemes reward these chains of cause and effect.

cites.quote: Increased digital awareness leads to increased/better infrastructure// more investment in IT (accept personal equivalences) (1) which then leads to increased digital awareness (1)

points.heading: Show the links
points.text: Cover good and bad sides where they exist. A June 2024 examiner report says full marks were possible without both. Some mark schemes cap an answer that covers only one side or one item.

cites.quote: While it was possible to gain full credit without doing so, a full analysis should have given details of both ‘for’ and ‘against’ the use of the waterfall method in the question scenario
Max 4 for all lossless or for all lossy

points.heading: Reach the effect the question asks for
points.text: Write about the effect the question asks for. If it asks about risks to an economy or effects on an image, every point must reach that.

cites.quote: references to a reduction in file size without an accompanying consequence on the image itself did not answer the question.

points.heading: Reach the effect the question asks for
points.text: Keep to the exact focus of the question. Avoid empty phrases like 'looks better'.

cites.quote: Vague references to ‘vector graphics make the site look better’ or ‘look attractive to students’ did not gain credit.

points.heading: Reach the effect the question asks for
points.text: Read the whole question. If it names some tools and asks about other ones, the named tools earn nothing.

cites.quote: a significant number of a candidates included the tools mentioned in the question in their answer, which did not gain them credit.

question.quote: Bitmap images can be compressed when stored and used on computer systems. Analyse the effects of the two main methods of image compression on a bitmap image.

strong.sentence: The two main methods of image compression are lossless compression and lossy compression.

earns.quote: (The two methods are) lossless compression and lossy compression

strong.sentence: Lossless compression stores all the image information exactly, because it removes no image information.

earns.quote: All image information is stored exactly/no image information is removed

strong.sentence: As a result, the computer can recreate the image perfectly, with no difference from the original.

earns.quote: Image is/can be recreated perfectly/with no difference from the original

strong.sentence: Lossy compression loses information during compression, and you cannot get that information back.

earns.quote: Information is lost during compression and is not/cannot be replaced

strong.sentence: Because of this, the image loses quality and may look blurred or blocky.
The quality gets worse each time you compress and save the image again, so an image that someone edits many times keeps losing detail.

earns.quote: Image quality is further degraded/reduced with repeated compression/decompression/saving and opening (1st)

weak.answer: Compression makes the file size smaller, so the image takes up less storage space and is quicker to send by email. Lossy makes the file smaller than lossless.
weak.why: It talks about file size and sending time. The question asked about the effect on the image.

basis.quote: references to a reduction in file size without an accompanying consequence on the image itself did not answer the question.
